$comment: Dev-tree advisories that have been looked at and accepted for now. Read by
scripts/check-audit.mjs; anything not listed here fails the supply-chain job.
Rules: `id` is the GHSA identifier, not the npm advisory number. `why` is
the actual reasoning, not a restatement of the title. `expires` is the date
the decision stops being valid, after which the gate fails until somebody
looks again — an allow-list without expiry dates is just a mute button.
There is no equivalent file for the production tree. An advisory that can
reach a user is a release decision and has no allow-list.
Note that `npm audit`'s headline count is packages, not advisories: it said
6 on 2026-08-12 while there were 7 distinct GHSAs, because three separate
vite advisories collapse into one line of its human-readable output.
Four of those seven — the three vite advisories and the nested esbuild one —
were removed on 2026-08-16 because they were fixed, not because they lapsed.
`overrides.vite` in package.json pins vite ^6.4.3 under vitepress, which
carries esbuild ^0.25. The reasoning is in ADR-0005's amendment; the lesson
is that a transitive advisory has two escape routes, and the first pass only
checked one of them.
The two serialize-javascript entries went the same way on 2026-08-27. When
they were written the fixed line (7.x) was recorded as out of reach because
mocha pins serialize-javascript@^6.0.2 — the parent-can't-move argument the
vite amendment warns about. serialize-javascript 7.0.5 fixed both advisories
(GHSA-5C6J-R48X-RMVQ, GHSA-QJ8W-GFJ5-8C6V) and has no dependencies and a
node >=20 floor, so `overrides.serialize-javascript` pins ^7.0.5 under mocha
and both alerts clear. Normal CI does not exercise this pin (mocha loads
serialize-javascript only in --parallel mode, and every job runs serially);
cover is npm audit plus a one-time mocha --parallel run. See ADR-0005's
2026-08-27 amendments.
On 2026-09-02 six more dev-tree advisories appeared, all transitive under
@vscode/vsce (the packaging tool, never shipped): qs 6.15.3 carried
GHSA-4MJR-XMP4-GH2G and GHSA-X5FP-WJ9C-MXMX (moderate, denial of service),
fixed in 6.16.0; fast-uri 3.1.5 carried GHSA-5JGF-P345-68V8,
GHSA-F65P-4M7J-42XC, GHSA-FPH4-WMHF-6FWF and GHSA-JQFF-G426-HQXP (high, host
confusion / SSRF), fixed in 3.1.6. Both fixed lines are in range for their
parents (typed-rest-client wants qs ^6.9.1; ajv wants fast-uri ^3.0.1), so
`overrides.qs` ^6.16.0 and `overrides.fast-uri` ^3.1.6 clear all six via the
child-override route with no entry here. Landed in the 5d-ii PR (#89).
That leaves one entry, the low diff advisory.

allowed.why: Reached only through mocha, which pins diff@^7; the fixed line is diff@8.0.3 and latest is 9.0.0, so the child-override route that cleared serialize-javascript exists here too — a two-major jump in the package mocha uses to render assertion diffs, taken for a low-severity denial of service in patch parsing that Dependabot itself auto-dismissed, on input that is our own test files. Not worth the override; kept here and revisited when mocha 12 (currently rc) ships with diff@^8 on its own. `npm audit fix --force` still proposes mocha@11.3.0, a downgrade that fixes nothing.
